findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 (P2, `if allowed {`) — A cached permission map that does not cover each newly checked resource falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, so a user with one scoped grant causes a permission-store query per distinct denied dashboard or folder instead of reusing the 30-second map, creating an unbounded high-cardinality database query pattern.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 (P2, `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`) — Concatenating two independently user-controlled UID fields with an unescaped underscore makes `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` share one denial entry, so a denial for one dashboard/folder pair can incorrectly deny the other for the cache TTL.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The new denial key is built from raw `checkReq.UserUID` before `GetUserIdentifiers` canonicalizes numeric IDs, so equivalent `user:<internal-id>` and `user:<uid>` requests create separate negative-cache entries and the latter still queries the permission store within the TTL (severity P2, confidence 90%).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — The only negative-cache test manually invokes `s.permDenialCache.Set(...)` instead of exercising `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`, so the suite does not verify that a real uncached denial is recorded and short-circuits the next Check (severity P2, confidence 97%).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Severity P1 (confidence 99%): `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` omits identity type, so a denied `anonymous:0` dashboard-read check writes the same 30-second denial key later read by permitted `render:0`, causing renderer requests to return false without reaching its wildcard grant.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — [P2] `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` ambiguously joins name and parent (for example, `a_b`/`c` and `a`/`b_c`), so a denial cached for one valid foldered resource makes the other return false without an authorization lookup for 30 seconds.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — [P3] `cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(ctx, checkReq.Namespace, checkReq.IdentityType, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action)` discards identity-resolution errors before the fallback repeats `GetUserIdentifiers` through `getIdentityPermissions` at line 139, doubling a timing-out downstream lookup and consuming the request deadline (with the same path in List at lines 180/186).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — [P2] The added explicit-denial case pre-populates `permDenialCache` and calls `Check` only once, so it never verifies that a real denial executes `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` and suppresses the next lookup; deleting the new write path still passes.

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 (P2, `if allowed {`) — A cached permission map that does not cover each newly checked resource falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, so a user with one scoped grant causes a permission-store query per distinct denied dashboard or folder instead of reusing the 30-second map, creating an unbounded high-cardinality database query pattern.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the caching logic. Looking at the diff, when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cached permissions and checkPermission returns allowed=false, it falls through to getIdentityPermissions which will fetch fresh permissions from the database. However, getIdentityPermissions then caches those permissions via permCache.Set (line 363 in the original code flow). The permDenialCache is also set for denied requests (line 153), preventing repeated queries for the same denial. The 'unbounded high-cardinality database query pattern' claim is incorrect because: 1) The denial cache prevents repeated queries for the same resource, 2) The permission cache is populated after the first database query, and 3) The singleflight group prevents concurrent duplicate queries. The finding describes a theoretical concern that doesn't match the actual implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The new denial key is built from raw `checkReq.UserUID` before `GetUserIdentifiers` canonicalizes numeric IDs, so equivalent `user:<internal-id>` and `user:<uid>` requests create separate negative-cache entries and the latter still queries the permission store within the TTL (severity P2, confidence 90%).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the Check function, the permDenialKey is constructed using checkReq.UserUID directly (line 116), before GetUserIdentifiers is called to canonicalize the user ID. Looking at the diff, getCachedIdentityPermissions (lines 339-373) does call GetUserIdentifiers to get the canonical UID before building the cache key, but the denial cache key at line 116 uses the raw checkReq.UserUID. This means if a user is identified by internal ID in one request and by UID in another, they would have different denial cache keys, causing cache misses and redundant database queries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — The only negative-cache test manually invokes `s.permDenialCache.Set(...)` instead of exercising `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`, so the suite does not verify that a real uncached denial is recorded and short-circuits the next Check (severity P2, confidence 97%).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' at line 973 manually sets the denial cache entry rather than testing the full flow where a denial is computed and then cached. Looking at the diff, the production code at lines 150-152 shows `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }`, but no test exercises this path and then verifies a subsequent Check is short-circuited. This is a valid test coverage gap for newly added caching logic - the test only verifies reading from the denial cache, not the write-then-read cycle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — Severity P1 (confidence 99%): `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` omits identity type, so a denied `anonymous:0` dashboard-read check writes the same 30-second denial key later read by permitted `render:0`, causing renderer requests to return false without reaching its wildcard grant.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that anonymous and render service identities could collide on the same cache key. However, looking at the diff, render service (TypeRenderService) returns early in getCachedIdentityPermissions with 'return nil, cache.ErrNotFound' and never uses the permission cache at all. Additionally, the denial cache is only set after checkPermission returns false, and render service permissions are handled separately via getIdentityPermissions which returns wildcard permissions directly. The cache key collision scenario described cannot actually occur because render service bypasses the cache entirely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — [P2] `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` ambiguously joins name and parent (for example, `a_b`/`c` and `a`/`b_c`), so a denial cached for one valid foldered resource makes the other return false without an authorization lookup for 30 seconds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the cache key function `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses underscore as a delimiter between all components: `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. This creates ambiguity - for example, if name='a_b' and parent='c', the key would be the same as name='a' and parent='b_c'. This could cause incorrect cache hits where a denial for one resource incorrectly denies access to a different resource. The diff shows this function is used in service.go for caching permission denials, and the cache has a 30-second TTL (shortCacheTTL). This is a real correctness bug that could cause authorization failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — [P3] `cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(ctx, checkReq.Namespace, checkReq.IdentityType, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action)` discards identity-resolution errors before the fallback repeats `GetUserIdentifiers` through `getIdentityPermissions` at line 139, doubling a timing-out downstream lookup and consuming the request deadline (with the same path in List at lines 180/186).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that getCachedIdentityPermissions at line 123 calls GetUserIdentifiers internally (line 351-353 in the diff), and if that fails, the error is discarded (only cache miss is checked). Then getIdentityPermissions at line 139 is called, which through getUserPermissions also calls GetUserIdentifiers again (line 376). If GetUserIdentifiers is timing out or failing, this results in the same failing call being made twice, consuming request deadline. The same pattern exists in List where getCachedIdentityPermissions is called at line 180 and getIdentityPermissions at line 186. This is a real correctness/performance bug where identity resolution errors cause redundant failing calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — [P2] The added explicit-denial case pre-populates `permDenialCache` and calls `Check` only once, so it never verifies that a real denial executes `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` and suppresses the next lookup; deleting the new write path still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap. Looking at the test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' (lines 973-995), it pre-populates permDenialCache with a denial entry and then calls Check once, verifying the denial is returned. However, this test doesn't verify the write path - it doesn't test that when a Check results in denial (after database lookup), the code at lines 153-155 actually writes to permDenialCache. A test that removes the Set call at line 154 would still pass this test case. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added logic, though the test does verify the read path works correctly.
